Chapter 10: The Ongoing Work of Being Human.
Healing—funny thing is, it's not some final stop on a map, is it? It's more like a journey you take every single day. Showing up, being honest with yourself, and choosing compassion, even when it’s hard. That’s what keeps it going.
The therapist saw this in her clients, and honestly, in herself too. There weren’t any finish lines or shiny certificates handed out. Instead, it was about the quiet, steady work of living each day with a little more courage and authenticity.
There was one client who, after months of real effort in therapy, found herself slipping back into some old patterns. She felt discouraged—like maybe she’d failed. But you know what she discovered? Setbacks are just part of the ride. Progress isn’t about getting everything perfect. It’s about being willing to keep trying, no matter what.
Another client had made some huge changes in his life. And then he started to worry—what now? What if all that progress just slipped away? In therapy, he explored how to hold onto those gains. Things like building simple routines, reaching out for support, and practicing a little self-care. It’s all about finding what keeps you grounded.
And the therapist? She kept doing her own work, too. She noticed how quickly self-criticism could sneak in, or how easy it was to expect herself to have it all figured out. But she also learned just how important self-compassion really is—to let herself be a work in progress, just like everyone else.
Therapy became a space to celebrate the wins, grieve the losses, and just wade through the messiness that is life. It’s a reminder that everyone—yes, everyone—is doing the best they can. We all have moments of doubt, and we all struggle sometimes.
The truth is, the work of being human? It’s never really finished. But it’s always, always worth doing.
